diffs.diff: maximum supply: part 5.5 V, datasheet reading 4.5 V
diffs.evidence: The model's vmax is for the SparkFun PRT-20680 v1.2 board's VCC header pin, which only feeds the I2C/alert pull-ups. SparkFun hookup guide: "VCC pin is connected to the I2C and alert pull-up resistors. This voltage input pin is different from the battery input pin. The maximum voltage that can be connected to this pin is 5.5V. This is typically 3.3V." This matches the chip datasheet's recommended operating condition for the pins those pull-ups drive: "Data I/O Pins QSTRT, SDA, SCL, ALRT ... -0.3 ... +5.5 V". The 4.5 V figure is the chip's VDD ("Supply Voltage VDD +2.5 ... +4.5 V"), which on this board comes from the battery on the JST/+ - pads, not from the VCC header. The model already states the 2.5-4.5 V battery/VDD range in the description, build notes and SKILL.md.
